To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

cholesterol is required for both virus entry by fusion and virus exit by budding, and that the cholesterol dependence of these processes can be modulated by the E1 224-235 region of the spike protein.

the alphaviruses SFV and SIN require cholesterol for both virus entry (fusion) and exit (budding) from cells, and that a single amino acid change in the E1 225-235 region of the spike protein of both viruses can modulate the cholesterol dependence of entry and exit.

Sindbis virus (a distantly related alphavirus to Semliki Forest Virus) is cholesterol dependent for both entry and exit and that the E1 spike protein region that confers cholesterol dependence in Semliki ForestVirus can also modulate cholesterol dependence in Sindbis virus.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of cholesterol and the spike protein in the entry and budding of enveloped viruses.
the entry and exit mechanisms of alphaviruses and how these processes are affected by cholesterol.
the role of cholesterol and the E1 225 region in the entry and budding of alphaviruses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
alphavirus fusion and exit are both cholesterol dependent.
cholesterol is required for alphavirus infection and is involved in both the entry and exit steps.
alphaviruses, including SFV and SIN, are cholesterol dependent for virus entry and exit and that the E1 225 to 235 region is involved in cholesterol dependence of both entry and exit.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cholesterol dependence for both virus fusion with and exit from the cell membrane can be modulated in alphaviruses by the amino acid sequence of a single region within E1.
SIN, like SFV, is a cholesterol-dependent virus, and the SFV E1 226 sequence is important for the cholesterol dependence of SFV.
the E1 227 region of SFV, and the corresponding E1 226 of SIN, are critical for cholesterol dependence of virus entry and exit.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the E1 227 region of the alphavirus E1 glycoprotein is a critical determinant of cholesterol dependence for virus entry and exit and is a potential target for antiviral drug development.
cholesterol is a requirement for both entry and exit of alphaviruses, and that this is a general feature of the virus group.
cholesterol plays an essential role in the life cycle of alphaviruses.
